subject: Business Models
title: Carbon Credit Marketplaces
description: A micro-lesson that makes Carbon Credit Marketplaces usable.

hook.text: Companies pay $50/ton to offset carbon emissions. The voluntary carbon market is worth $2 billion and growing.

buildup.text: Carbon credits let polluters pay others to reduce emissions: reforestation, clean energy, or methane capture.

discovery.text: Marketplaces like Xpansiv and CBL trade carbon credits like commodities. Prices fluctuate with policy and demand.

twist.text: Many carbon credits are fraudulent. One study found 90% of rainforest credits didn't represent real emission reductions.

climax.text: Carbon markets can fight climate change—but only with rigorous verification. The model's integrity is its value.

punchline.text: $2B market, 90% of credits dubious. Carbon markets need trust to work.

quiz.question: What major problem plagues carbon credit markets?
options: Many credits don't represent real emission reductions

details.summary: Carbon credit marketplaces enable companies to buy and sell verified carbon offsets representing measurable greenhouse gas reductions. Compliance markets enforce government-mandated emission caps while voluntary markets let companies purchase offsets to meet sustainability pledges and net-zero.
details.whyItMatters: The carbon credit market exceeded 900 billion dollars in 2023 and is growing rapidly as governments tighten emission regulations and corporations face pressure from investors and consumers to demonstrate climate action through verified carbon.
takeaways: Companies buy credits representing verified carbon emission reductions
Compliance markets enforce regulatory caps; voluntary markets address pledges
The market exceeded 900 billion dollars in 2023 and is growing rapidly

faq.question: How do carbon credit marketplaces generate revenue?
faq.answer: Marketplace platforms charge transaction fees on credit trades. Verification companies earn fees for auditing emission reduction claims. Project developers earn from selling credits generated by their conservation or renewable energy projects..

faq.question: What are the biggest criticisms of carbon credit markets?
faq.answer: Many credits represent emission reductions that would have happened anyway with questionable additionality. Verification standards vary in rigor, allowing greenwashing. Some offset projects fail to deliver permanent reductions..
